headline: Every major sits below its own week and above its own month, and the whales are picking the down window to move onto exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's cleaner than the daily red suggests. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB are all above their 200-day lines with golden crosses in place, DOGE and ADA are not. That's five of seven majors in a constructive long-term posture, which is a different market than the widespread red across the 24-hour column implies. BTC sits 38.2% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 48.3% off its high, and the smaller names are further still. So the tape is: long-term structure intact for most, but nobody is anywhere near their highs, and today everybody is down together.

Momentum is where it gets interesting. RSI readings across the board sit in a narrow 50-57 band, essentially neutral, not overbought, not oversold. But MACD is below signal on every single asset listed. That's a trend that's resting or rolling over on the daily timeframe even as price sits well above the 200-day average and up double digits on the month (BTC +20.7%, ETH +27.5%, SOL +35.5% over 30 days). Put plainly: the medium-term trend is still up, the near-term momentum has gone flat to soft, and the last 24 hours (BTC -1.5%, ETH -1.4%, SOL -1.8%, XRP -2.2%, BNB -1.8%, DOGE -2.5%) is the market working that off. Total market cap fell 4.84% on the day, so this wasn't a one-coin story.

Positioning tells you who's paying for what. BTC funding on OKX is positive but mild at 11% annualized, longs paying shorts to stay in the trade. ETH funding has actually flipped negative (-10.3% annualized), meaning shorts are now paying longs there, a small but real divergence from BTC. SOL and DOGE funding are also negative. Long/short account ratios are lopsided toward longs everywhere (BTC 1.53, XRP 2.56, DOGE 4.11), and liquidations in the last few hours have hit longs far harder than shorts: BTC longs lost $1.34M against just $38.7k in short liquidations, XRP longs lost $629.6k versus $15k shorts. That's a crowd leaning long getting leaned on, which is a fragile combination even without funding being extreme.

Flows add a layer of disagreement worth naming directly. BTC spot ETFs posted a $120.2M outflow on Sep 9, but the five-session net is a positive $839.7M, a case where the daily print and the short trailing window point opposite ways (the data flags this explicitly). ETH ETFs are cleaner: $34.7M in on the day, $129.5M over five sessions, same direction both ways. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $157.9M net onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, mostly BTC into Coinbase Institutional, and the weekly series shows the pattern isn't new: three of the last four tracked weeks (ending Aug 20, Aug 27, and now Sep 10) show net flow onto exchanges, with only the week ending Sep 3 breaking that pattern with $440M off exchanges. Stablecoin float, the dry powder sitting in cash-equivalents, is up 1.66% over 30 days to $310.2B, so the ammunition is growing even as coins move toward exchanges rather than away from them.

Sentiment sits at 69, Greed, comfortably inside its own 30-day range of 27 to 74 but toward the top of it. That's a crowd feeling good on a day the market cap fell nearly 5%, funding on several assets is going negative, and BTC just posted its third onto-exchanges week out of four. The gauge and the tape aren't agreeing right now, and when they don't, the tape is the one with a paper trail. What's worth watching from here: whether ETH funding staying negative alongside a growing OI turns into an actual short squeeze setup or just fades, whether the next weekly whale print flips back to off-exchanges the way it briefly did in the week ending Sep 3, and whether BTC's ETF flow settles toward the five-session inflow or the single-day outflow as more prints come in.
